Commentary of al-Jaza'iri (Aysar al-Tafasir) on surah 34, verses 1–2:

Explanation of the words:

Al-hamdu lillah (all praise is due to Allah): that is, the attribution of beauty is obligatory for Allah and He alone deserves it.

Alladhi lahu ma fi as-samawati wa ma fi al-ard (to Him belongs whatever is in the heavens and whatever is on the earth): that is, by creation, ownership, disposal and management.

Wa lahu al-hamdu fi al-akhirah (and to Him belongs praise in the Hereafter): that is, His friends (awliya') will praise Him there while they are in the gardens of Paradise, just as praise is His in this world.

Wa huwa al-hakim al-khabir (and He is the All-Wise, the All-Aware): that is, wise in His actions, aware of the conditions of His servants.

Ya'lamu ma yalij fi al-ard (He knows what enters into the earth): that is, what goes into it of rain, the dead, and treasures.

Wa ma yakhruju minha (and what comes out of it): that is, of plants, springs and minerals.

Wa ma yanzilu mina as-sama' (and what descends from the sky): that is, of angels, rain, provisions and the like.

Wa ma ya'ruju fiha (and what ascends into it): that is, what rises up into it of angels, the deeds of the servants, and their souls after death.

Wa huwa ar-rahim al-ghafur (and He is the Most Merciful, the Most Forgiving): that is, merciful to the believers and forgiving to those who repent.

Meaning of the two verses:

He, exalted is He, informs His servants that He alone has complete and perfect praise and thanks, to the exclusion of all His creatures. None deserves praise in reality except Him. As for His creatures, whatever is praised in them is from Allah's giving and bestowal upon them; so none deserves praise in truth except Allah. As He has informed us, the consequence of His being praised and thanked is that to Him belongs whatever is in the heavens and the earth, by creation, ownership, management and disposal, and none other than Him has any share in that. This is in this world. ﴿And to Him belongs praise in the Hereafter﴾, when He honours His friends, settling them in the Abode of Peace, and they praise Him for that. ﴿And they will say, "Praise be to Allah, who has fulfilled His promise to us and made us inherit the land, to dwell in Paradise wherever we will"﴾ [az-Zumar: 74]. His saying, ﴿And He is the All-Wise, the All-Aware﴾, refers to His disposal of the affairs of His servants and of all His creatures and their management; He is the All-Aware of their conditions, the All-Knowing of their outward and inward attributes.

His saying ﴿He knows what enters into the earth﴾ means what goes into the earth of rain, treasures and the dead; ﴿and what comes out of it﴾ means from the earth, plants, minerals and waters; and what descends from the sky of rain, angels and provisions; ﴿and what ascends into it﴾ means what rises up of angels and the deeds of the servants. He, together with power, majesty and perfection, is alone the Most Merciful to His believing servants and the Most Forgiving to those who repent. By these attributes, established for the Divine Essence, which are attributes of majesty, beauty and perfection, the Lord, exalted is He, deserves to be worshipped to the exclusion of all others. Thus every worship directed to other than Him is false, reprehensible and falsehood, which must be abandoned and renounced, and its doer condemned until he abandons it and renounces it.

Guidance from the two verses:

1- The obligation to praise and thank Allah with the heart, tongue, limbs and body.

2- Clarification that praise is valid only together with what it requires of majesty and beauty.

3- Only Allah, glorified and exalted, is praised in the Hereafter.

4- Clarification of Allah's knowledge of the outward and inward in all His creation.

5- Affirmation of the Oneness of Allah in His lordship and His divinity.

Commentary of al-Jaza'iri (Aysar al-Tafasir) on surah 34, verses 3–6:

Explanation of the words:

Lā ta'tīnā al-sā'ah (the Hour will not come upon us): i.e., the Resurrection (al-qiyamah).

Lā ya'zubu 'anh (not hidden from Him): i.e., not absent from Him.

Mithqāl dharrah (the weight of an atom): i.e., the weight of an atom, the smallest ant.

Wa-lā aṣghara min dhālika wa-lā akbar (nor smaller than that, nor greater): smaller than the atom, nor greater than it.

Illā fī kitāb mubīn (except that it is in a clear Book): i.e., it exists in the Preserved Tablet (al-lawh al-maḥfūẓ), written therein.

Li-yajziya alladhīna āmanū (that He may reward those who believe): i.e., He recorded it in the Preserved Tablet so that they may be called to account by it and so that He may reward its doer.

Wa-alladhīna sa'aw fī āyātinā (and those who strive against Our signs): i.e., those who worked to nullify them and exerted their utmost effort in that.

Mu'ājizīn (striving to frustrate): i.e., contending against Us, thinking that they could overpower Us, and that they would escape Us so that We would not resurrect them, call them to account, or reward them.

'Adhābun min rijzin alīm (a painful torment of abominable punishment): i.e., a torment of the most vile and wretched kind.

Wa-yarā alladhīna ūtū al-'ilm (and those who have been given knowledge will know): i.e., those who were given knowledge, namely the scholars of the People of the Book, such as 'Abdullah ibn Salam and his companions.

Alladhī unzila ilayka min rabbika huwa al-ḥaqq (what has been sent down to you from your Lord is the truth): i.e., the Qur'an is the truth revealed by Allah, the Exalted.

Wa-yahdī ilā ṣirāṭ al-'azīz al-ḥamīd (and guides to the path of the Mighty, the Praiseworthy): i.e., the Qur'an guides to the path of Allah that leads to His pleasure and His noble proximity, and that path is Islam. Al-'Azīz is the Possessor of might, and al-Ḥamīd is the One who is praised.

Meaning of the verses:

After the preceding verses established the Oneness of Allah in His lordship and His divinity, He, may He be exalted, in these verses affirms the doctrine of the Resurrection and the Recompense. He said, relating what was said by those who denied the Resurrection and the Recompense: ﴿And those who disbelieve say, "The Hour will not come upon us."﴾ This is a denial from them of the Resurrection, since the Hour is the hour of annihilation and the Resurrection follows it. He commanded His Messenger to say to them: ﴿Yes, by my Lord, it will surely come upon you﴾, i.e., he swears to them by Allah, his Lord and the Lord of everything, that it will surely come upon them, whether they love it or dislike it. Then the Lord, blessed and exalted, praised Himself with the attribute of knowledge, since the Resurrection depends on knowledge just as it depends on power, and power is established, since He created them, provided for them, and causes them to die. Thus He mentioned that He is the Knower of the unseen, which is everything that is hidden in the heavens and on the earth. He informed that there is not hidden from His knowledge the weight of an atom in the heavens or on the earth, i.e., the weight of an atom, nor anything smaller than the atom or greater, except that it is in a clear Book, i.e., a manifest one, which is the Preserved Tablet in which Allah wrote all the events of the world. There is no movement or stillness that occurs or will occur in the universe except that it has its form and its time in the Preserved Tablet.

This is what the third verse contains. And His saying, may He be exalted, in verse [4]: ﴿That He may reward those who believe and do righteous deeds﴾, i.e., the wisdom behind recording events, small and great, and behind the final Resurrection, is that Allah, may He be exalted, rewards those who believe, i.e., who affirm Allah and His Messenger, and do righteous deeds, which are performing the obligatory duties and the sunnah practices, with the reward for them mentioned in His saying: ﴿Those will have forgiveness﴾, i.e., for their sins, ﴿and provision noble﴾ in Paradise. And His saying in verse [5]: ﴿And those who strive against Our signs﴾ states the recompense of the disbelievers after having stated the recompense of the believers, that recompense which is the wisdom and the cause of the Resurrection and of recording deeds in the Preserved Tablet. He said: ﴿And those who strive against Our signs, seeking to frustrate [them]﴾, i.e., those who exerted their utmost effort to nullify the signs of Allah, saying that they are the speech of soothsayers, that they are poetry, and the fables of the ancients, so that they would not believe or affirm Allah's oneness. Those are far removed in baseness and degradation, and for them is a punishment: ﴿a painful torment of abominable punishment﴾. Rijz means the worst and most severe punishment, and alīm means full of pain and severe distress.

His saying, may He be exalted, in verse [6]: ﴿And those who have been given knowledge will see﴾, i.e., the scholars of the People of the Book, such as 'Abdullah ibn Salam and his companions from among the believers of the People of the Book, will know that ﴿what has been sent down to you from your Lord, which is the Noble Qur'an, is the truth, and it guides to the path of the Mighty, the Praiseworthy.﴾ The knowledge of the People of the Book that the Qur'an is true results from its agreement with what is in the Book of Allah, the Torah, regarding the doctrine of divine decree and the recording of deeds, both minor and major, in the Preserved Tablet, by which Allah, may He be exalted, will recompense believers and disbelievers on the Day of Resurrection.

This is what the last verse [6] indicates, namely His saying: ﴿And see﴾, i.e., and let know ﴿those who have been given knowledge that what has been sent down to you from your Lord is the truth, and it guides to the path of the Mighty, the Praiseworthy﴾, and that is Islam.

Guidance from the verses:

1- Establishing the doctrine of the Resurrection and the Recompense after establishing the Oneness of divinity.

2- Establishing the doctrine of divine decree and destiny, and the recording of deeds and events in the Preserved Tablet.

3- Seeking the testimony of the People of the Book to the truth of Islam, and obtaining it, since the Torah agrees with the Qur'an.

4- Establishing prophethood, since the Qur'an is the branch of the Messenger's prophethood (ﷺ) and its established proof.

After the preceding verses established the Oneness of Allah in His lordship and His divinity, He, may He be exalted, in these verses affirms the doctrine of the Resurrection and the Recompense. He said, relating what was said by those who denied the Resurrection and the Recompense: ﴿And those who disbelieve say, "The Hour will not come upon us."﴾ This is a denial from them of the Resurrection, since the Hour is the hour of annihilation and the Resurrection follows it. He commanded His Messenger to say to them: ﴿Yes, by my Lord, it will surely come upon you﴾, i.e., he swears to them by Allah, his Lord and the Lord of everything, that it will surely come upon them, whether they love it or dislike it. Then the Lord, blessed and exalted, praised Himself with the attribute of knowledge, since the Resurrection depends on knowledge just as it depends on power, and power is established, since He created them, provided for them, and causes them to die. Thus He mentioned that He is the Knower of the unseen, which is everything that is hidden in the heavens and on the earth. He informed that there is not hidden from His knowledge the weight of an atom in the heavens or on the earth, i.e., the weight of an atom, nor anything smaller than the atom or greater, except that it is in a clear Book, i.e., a manifest one, which is the Preserved Tablet in which Allah wrote all the events of the world. There is no movement or stillness that occurs or will occur in the universe except that it has its form and its time in the Preserved Tablet.

This is what the third verse contains. And His saying, may He be exalted, in verse [4]: ﴿That He may reward those who believe and do righteous deeds﴾, i.e., the wisdom behind recording events, small and great, and behind the final Resurrection, is that Allah, may He be exalted, rewards those who believe, i.e., who affirm Allah and His Messenger, and do righteous deeds, which are performing the obligatory duties and the sunnah practices, with the reward for them mentioned in His saying: ﴿Those will have forgiveness﴾, i.e., for their sins, ﴿and provision noble﴾ in Paradise. And His saying in verse [5]: ﴿And those who strive against Our signs﴾ states the recompense of the disbelievers after having stated the recompense of the believers, that recompense which is the wisdom and the cause of the Resurrection and of recording deeds in the Preserved Tablet. He said: ﴿And those who strive against Our signs, seeking to frustrate [them]﴾, i.e., those who exerted their utmost effort to nullify the signs of Allah, saying that they are the speech of soothsayers, that they are poetry, and the fables of the ancients, so that they would not believe or affirm Allah's oneness. Those are far removed in baseness and degradation, and for them is a punishment: ﴿a painful torment of abominable punishment﴾. Rijz means the worst and most severe punishment, and alīm means full of pain and severe distress.

His saying, may He be exalted, in verse [6]: ﴿And those who have been given knowledge will see﴾, i.e., the scholars of the People of the Book, such as 'Abdullah ibn Salam and his companions from among the believers of the People of the Book, will know that ﴿what has been sent down to you from your Lord, which is the Noble Qur'an, is the truth, and it guides to the path of the Mighty, the Praiseworthy.﴾ The knowledge of the People of the Book that the Qur'an is true results from its agreement with what is in the Book of Allah, the Torah, regarding the doctrine of divine decree and the recording of deeds, both minor and major, in the Preserved Tablet, by which Allah, may He be exalted, will recompense believers and disbelievers on the Day of Resurrection.

This is what the last verse [6] indicates, namely His saying: ﴿And see﴾, i.e., and let know ﴿those who have been given knowledge that what has been sent down to you from your Lord is the truth, and it guides to the path of the Mighty, the Praiseworthy﴾, and that is Islam.

Guidance from the verses:

1- Establishing the doctrine of the Resurrection and the Recompense after establishing the Oneness of divinity.

2- Establishing the doctrine of divine decree and destiny, and the recording of deeds and events in the Preserved Tablet.

3- Seeking the testimony of the People of the Book to the truth of Islam, and obtaining it, since the Torah agrees with the Qur'an.

4- Establishing prophethood, since the Qur'an is the branch of the Messenger's prophethood (ﷺ) and its established proof.

Commentary of al-Jaza'iri (Aysar al-Tafasir) on surah 34, verses 7–9:

Explanation of the words:

﴿And those who disbelieved said﴾: that is, some of them said to others, in a manner of wonder.

﴿Shall we direct you to a man﴾: that is, Muhammad (ﷺ).

﴿When you are completely torn apart﴾: that is, you are cut into complete pieces.

﴿Indeed, you will be in a new creation﴾: that is, you will be resurrected in a new creation, with nothing of you diminished.

﴿Or has he invented about Allah a lie, or is there in him madness?﴾: that is, madness that imagines this to him.

﴿But they who do not believe in the Hereafter are in torment and far error﴾: that is, the matter is not as the polytheists say, that the Messenger fabricated it or is mad; rather, the established and actual fact is that those who do not believe in the Hereafter are in torment in the Hereafter, and in far error in this world.

﴿Have they not seen﴾: that is, have they not looked.

﴿to what is before them and what is behind them﴾: that is, from in front of them, behind them, above them and below them, since they are surrounded from every direction by the sky and the earth.

﴿Or We cause to fall upon them fragments from the sky﴾: that is, pieces; the plural of kisfah, meaning a piece.

﴿Indeed, in that is a sign﴾: that is, a clear sign and a decisive proof of Allah's power over them.

﴿for every servant who turns back in repentance﴾: that is, for every believer who turns back in repentance to his Lord, returning to Him in all his affairs.

Meaning of the verses:

The context continues in establishing the doctrine of resurrection and recompense. After Allah established it in the preceding verses, He here mentions what the polytheists say among themselves in mockery, derision and disbelief in the afterlife. So Allah, relating their speech, says: ﴿And those who disbelieved said﴾, and they are the polytheists of Makkah, that is, some of them to others, amazed, ﴿Shall we direct you to a man﴾, meaning Muhammad (ﷺ), ﴿who will inform you﴾, that is, tell you, that when you die and your flesh is torn apart and your bones are broken and you go into the earth as dust, you will be resurrected in a new creation, ﴿after you have been completely torn apart﴾, that is, utterly torn to pieces, so that nothing remains joined to another. ﴿Has he invented about Allah a lie﴾, that is, has Muhammad fabricated this statement against Allah, attributing it to Him, and claimed that He informed him of a new resurrection of people after their death for their reckoning and recompense?! ﴿Or is there in him madness﴾, that is, is there in him a touch of madness, so that it imagines to him the images of resurrection and what occurs in it, while he reports it and calls to belief in it? Here Allah refutes their lie and falsehood, saying: ﴿But they who do not believe in the Hereafter are in torment and far error﴾, that is, the matter is not as they say, that the Prophet fabricated a lie against Allah or that he is mad and imagined the resurrection to himself. Rather, the established and certain fact is that those who do not believe in the Hereafter will be in torment on the Day of Resurrection, and in far error today in this world, and their misfortune came to them from their denial of the Hereafter.

Then Allah says, threatening them so that they may refrain from ridiculing and mocking the Prophet (ﷺ): ﴿Have they not seen﴾, that is, are they blind that they have not seen ﴿to what is before them and what is behind them of the sky and the earth?﴾ Have they not looked at how they are surrounded from above, below, in front of them and behind them, that is, the earth beneath them and the sky above them? ﴿If We will, We cause the earth to swallow them﴾, so they would sink into it, ﴿or We cause to fall upon them fragments from the sky﴾, that is, pieces of the sky, so that He destroys them entirely and they find no escape. The answer is no, because however much they run fleeing, the sky is still above them and the earth beneath them, and Allah is dominant over them: whenever He wills, He causes the earth to swallow them or drops the sky upon them.

As for His saying: ﴿Indeed, in that is a sign for every servant who turns back in repentance﴾, that is, indeed in what has been mentioned, namely the encompassing of the sky and the earth and Allah's power to cause the earth to swallow whom He wills or to drop pieces of the sky upon whom He wills, there is a sign for them, a manifest indication of Allah's power to destroy whom He wills among those who disbelieved in Allah and His Messenger and denied meeting Him. That what has been mentioned is a sign specifically for every servant who turns back in repentance, rather than others, is because the one who turns back (munib) is one who returns to his Lord whenever he sins, repenting out of fear of his Lord. The fearful, God-conscious one is the one who finds the sign clear before him in the encompassing of the earth and sky around a person and Allah's power to make the earth swallow him or the sky fall upon him in pieces.

Guidance of the verses:

Among the guidance of these verses:

1- Clarification of what the polytheists were engaged in: mockery, denial and ridicule directed at the Prophet (ﷺ).

2- Affirmation of the resurrection, and that those who deny it are destined for punishment in it.

3- Drawing attention to Allah's all-encompassing power over the human being, so that he fears and dreads Allah, and thus believes in Him, worships Him and affirms His oneness.

4- The virtue of turning back to Allah and the nobility of the one who turns back. Repentance (inabah) is returning to Allah in repentance after sin and disobedience, and the munib is one who returns to his Lord in everything.

**Explanation of the words:**

﴿And We certainly gave David grace from Us﴾: that is, prophethood and kingship.

﴿O mountains, echo along with him﴾: that is, and We said, "O mountains, echo (the praise) along with him," meaning return with him in glorification.

﴿And the birds﴾: that is, and the birds also glorify along with him.

﴿And We made iron soft for him﴾: that is, We made it pliable for him like dough, which he kneads as he wishes.

﴿That make full coats of mail﴾: that is, long coats of armor that cover the body and protect against sword strikes.

﴿And calculate well the links﴾: that is, make the rivet suited to the ring, so that it is neither too thick nor too thin. That is, make the rivets proportionate to the rings, because a lack of proportion leads to a defective coat of mail that cannot be used.

﴿And for Solomon the wind: its morning course was a month's journey and its evening course a month's journey﴾: that is, We subjected the wind to Solomon, its morning course (from dawn until midday) covering a month's distance, and its evening course (from midday until night) likewise covering a month's distance.

﴿And We caused a fount of molten copper to flow for him﴾: that is, We caused a spring of brass to flow for him.

﴿And among the jinn were those who worked before him﴾: that is, whoever among them deviates from obeying Solomon and does not obey him, We will make him taste the punishment of the Blazing Fire.

﴿Places of worship﴾: plural of mihrab, a private chamber next to the mosque used for worship.

﴿Basins like reservoirs﴾: that is, large bowls, as large as the cisterns around wells into which water is collected.

﴿And cooking pots fixed firmly﴾: that is, large cooking pots that remain fixed on their athafi (stones supporting the pot) because of their size and are not moved.

﴿Except the creeping insect of the earth﴾: that is, the termite.

﴿Which ate away at his staff﴾: that is, his staff, in the language of Abyssinia (Ethiopia).

﴿Then when he fell﴾: that is, he fell to the ground dead.

﴿It became clear to the jinn﴾: that is, it was revealed to them and they came to know.

﴿The humiliating punishment﴾: this refers to serving Solomon in hard labor.

**Meaning of the verses:**

In this noble context, Allah, exalted is He, mentions the manifestations of His power and His favors upon His believing servants, encouraging obedience to Him and warning against disobeying Him. He says: ﴿And We certainly gave David grace from Us﴾, which was prophethood, the Zabur (Psalms, a book), and kingship. And We said to the mountains: ﴿O mountains, echo along with him﴾, that is, return the sound of his glorification, and We likewise commanded the birds, so whenever he glorified, the mountains and birds repeated his glorification. This is a subjugation that none can accomplish except Allah. And His saying: ﴿And We made iron soft for him﴾ is another favor, namely the subjugation of iron to him and its softening until it was as though it were dough that he could shape as he wished. We also said to him: make long, full coats of mail with which you can protect yourself in war, (and calculate well the links). His saying: ﴿And do righteous deeds﴾ means: act in obedience to Me and abandon disobedience to Me, so perform the obligations and duties and leave sins and prohibited acts. His saying: ﴿Indeed, I am Seeing of what you do﴾ contains both promise and warning, since knowledge of deeds entails reward for them if they are righteous and punishment for them if they are corrupt.

His exalted saying: ﴿And for Solomon the wind﴾, that is, We subjected the wind to Solomon son of David, ﴿its morning course was a month's journey and its evening course a month's journey﴾, that is, it covered the distance of a month in the morning and another in the evening, from midday until night, thus covering the journey of two months in a single day. This was because Solomon had a vessel made of wood, in which he would carry men and equipment, and the jinn would lift it from the ground. When it rose, a storm would come and carry it, then it would turn into a gentle breeze, and Solomon would direct the ship wherever he wished with everything it carried, and would land with it exactly like a spacecraft.

His exalted saying: ﴿And We caused a fount of molten copper to flow for him﴾, which is brass. Just as We made iron soft for David for crafting, We caused a spring of brass to flow for Solomon for his craft, so he could make whatever brass tools and implements he wished.

His exalted saying: ﴿And among the jinn﴾, that is, We subjected to Solomon a group of the jinn who worked before him, that is, in front of him and under his supervision, doing for him whatever he wished of worldly affairs, by the permission of their Lord, exalted is He, who is capable of subjecting whatever He wills to whomever He wills. His saying: ﴿And whoever of them deviates﴾, that is, whoever among the jinn deviates ﴿from Our command﴾, that is, from what We commanded them to do and charged them with, ﴿We will make him taste the punishment of the Blazing Fire﴾, and that will be on the Day of Resurrection. His saying: ﴿They made for him whatever he willed﴾ explains what is meant by ﴿those who worked before him﴾: places of worship, which were palaces or houses adjoining the mosque for worship in them, and statues, that is, images of brass or wood, since these were not forbidden in their law; and basins, the plural of jafna, which is a large dish large enough for ten eaters; ﴿like reservoirs﴾, that is, in their size, and the jabiyah is a basin into which the water of a well is poured and then used to irrigate crops; or ﴿cooking pots fixed firmly﴾, that is, they made for him huge cooking pots that were not moved but remained permanently placed on the athafi, and food was cooked in them while they stayed in their place, because of their size. The meaning of ﴿fixed firmly﴾ is: stable upon the athafi.

His exalted saying: ﴿Work, O family of David﴾, that is, We said to them: work, family of David, in gratitude, meaning do righteous deeds in thankfulness to Allah, exalted is He, for this bounty and favor, that is, establish prayer, give zakat, and obey your Lord in His commands and prohibitions; if you do so, that will be your gratitude to Allah for His blessings. It is narrated that when they were commanded with this, David (peace be upon him) said to his family: "Which of you will take over for me during the day, for I will take over for you during the night?" So they prayed to Allah in gratitude. Whatever hour of night or day you looked into their place of worship, you would see someone bowing or prostrating. It suffices as evidence that Solomon died while standing and praying in the mihrab. His exalted saying: ﴿And few of My servants are grateful﴾ is a statement of a reality, and the word of Allah, the Mighty, is true: those who are grateful to Allah for His blessings are few, in every time and place, because heedlessness has taken hold of hearts on the one hand, and because people are ignorant of their Lord and His favors on the other.

His exalted saying in verse [14]: ﴿Then when We decreed death for him﴾, that is, We caused him to die. Nothing indicated his death to them except a creature of the earth, namely the well-known termite, which ate away at his staff. When it had eaten it, he fell to the ground. That was because he had asked his Lord to conceal the news of his death from the jinn, so that people would know that the jinn do not know the unseen, as they claimed. He died while leaning on his staff, praying in his mihrab, while the jinn continued working, unaware of his death. When a period of time passed and the termite had eaten the staff, and Solomon fell to the ground, the jinn realized that if they had known the unseen, they would have known of Solomon's death, and they would not have remained for a long time in service and hard labor while unaware.

This is the meaning of His exalted saying: ﴿Then when We decreed death for him, nothing indicated to them his death except a creature of the earth eating away at his staff. So when he fell, the jinn realized that if they had known the unseen they would not have remained in the humiliating punishment﴾, as some of them had claimed. That is, the punishment that Solomon had inflicted upon them for their disobedience and rebellion against obedience.

**Guidance of the verses:**

1. Explanation of Allah's honoring of the family of David and of the signs that He granted to David and Solomon.
2. The virtue of manufacturing weapons and instruments of war for the purpose of jihad in the way of Allah.
3. Solomon's vessel preceded the modern aircraft by thousands of years.
4. The law of earlier communities (shar' man qablana) is law for us, except what is specified by evidence, such as the prohibition of images and statues for us, which was not prohibited for them.
5. The obligation of gratitude for blessings, and the most important means of showing gratitude is prayer and frequent performance of it.
6. Affirmation that knowledge of the unseen belongs to Allah alone.

**Explanation of the words:**

His exalted saying: ﴿And for Solomon the wind﴾, that is, We subjected the wind to Solomon son of David, ﴿its morning course was a month's journey and its evening course a month's journey﴾, that is, it covered the distance of a month in the morning and another in the evening, from midday until night, thus covering the journey of two months in a single day. This was because Solomon had a vessel made of wood, in which he would carry men and equipment, and the jinn would lift it from the ground. When it rose, a storm would come and carry it, then it would turn into a gentle breeze, and Solomon would direct the ship wherever he wished with everything it carried, and would land with it exactly like a spacecraft.

His exalted saying: ﴿And We caused a fount of molten copper to flow for him﴾, which is brass. Just as We made iron soft for David for crafting, We caused a spring of brass to flow for Solomon for his craft, so he could make whatever brass tools and implements he wished.

His exalted saying: ﴿And among the jinn﴾, that is, We subjected to Solomon a group of the jinn who worked before him, that is, in front of him and under his supervision, doing for him whatever he wished of worldly affairs, by the permission of their Lord, exalted is He, who is capable of subjecting whatever He wills to whomever He wills. His saying: ﴿And whoever of them deviates﴾, that is, whoever among the jinn deviates ﴿from Our command﴾, that is, from what We commanded them to do and charged them with, ﴿We will make him taste the punishment of the Blazing Fire﴾, and that will be on the Day of Resurrection. His saying: ﴿They made for him whatever he willed﴾ explains what is meant by ﴿those who worked before him﴾: places of worship, which were palaces or houses adjoining the mosque for worship in them, and statues, that is, images of brass or wood, since these were not forbidden in their law; and basins, the plural of jafna, which is a large dish large enough for ten eaters; ﴿like reservoirs﴾, that is, in their size, and the jabiyah is a basin into which the water of a well is poured and then used to irrigate crops; or ﴿cooking pots fixed firmly﴾, that is, they made for him huge cooking pots that were not moved but remained permanently placed on the athafi, and food was cooked in them while they stayed in their place, because of their size. The meaning of ﴿fixed firmly﴾ is: stable upon the athafi.

His exalted saying: ﴿Work, O family of David﴾, that is, We said to them: work, family of David, in gratitude, meaning do righteous deeds in thankfulness to Allah, exalted is He, for this bounty and favor, that is, establish prayer, give zakat, and obey your Lord in His commands and prohibitions; if you do so, that will be your gratitude to Allah for His blessings. It is narrated that when they were commanded with this, David (peace be upon him) said to his family: "Which of you will take over for me during the day, for I will take over for you during the night?" So they prayed to Allah in gratitude. Whatever hour of night or day you looked into their place of worship, you would see someone bowing or prostrating. It suffices as evidence that Solomon died while standing and praying in the mihrab. His exalted saying: ﴿And few of My servants are grateful﴾ is a statement of a reality, and the word of Allah, the Mighty, is true: those who are grateful to Allah for His blessings are few, in every time and place, because heedlessness has taken hold of hearts on the one hand, and because people are ignorant of their Lord and His favors on the other.

His exalted saying in verse [14]: ﴿Then when We decreed death for him﴾, that is, We caused him to die. Nothing indicated his death to them except a creature of the earth, namely the well-known termite, which ate away at his staff. When it had eaten it, he fell to the ground. That was because he had asked his Lord to conceal the news of his death from the jinn, so that people would know that the jinn do not know the unseen, as they claimed. He died while leaning on his staff, praying in his mihrab, while the jinn continued working, unaware of his death. When a period of time passed and the termite had eaten the staff, and Solomon fell to the ground, the jinn realized that if they had known the unseen, they would have known of Solomon's death, and they would not have remained for a long time in service and hard labor while unaware.

This is the meaning of His exalted saying: ﴿Then when We decreed death for him, nothing indicated to them his death except a creature of the earth eating away at his staff. So when he fell, the jinn realized that if they had known the unseen they would not have remained in the humiliating punishment﴾, as some of them had claimed. That is, the punishment that Solomon had inflicted upon them for their disobedience and rebellion against obedience.

**Guidance of the verses:**

1. Explanation of Allah's honoring of the family of David and of the signs that He granted to David and Solomon.
2. The virtue of manufacturing weapons and instruments of war for the purpose of jihad in the way of Allah.
3. Solomon's vessel preceded the modern aircraft by thousands of years.
4. The law of earlier communities (shar' man qablana) is law for us, except what is specified by evidence, such as the prohibition of images and statues for us, which was not prohibited for them.
5. The obligation of gratitude for blessings, and the most important means of showing gratitude is prayer and frequent performance of it.
6. Affirmation that knowledge of the unseen belongs to Allah alone.

Commentary of al-Jaza'iri (Aysar al-Tafasir) on surah 34, verses 15–19:

Explanation of the words:

Indeed there was for Saba' in their dwelling: that is, indeed there was for the tribe of Saba', the Yemeni people, in their dwelling.

A sign (ayah): that is, a sign of God's power, namely two gardens, one on the right and one on the left.

A good land and a Lord Forgiving: that is, its climate was good, far from plagues and their causes, and God is a Lord Forgiving.

But they turned away: that is, from thanking God and worshipping Him.

The flood of al-'Arim: that is, the breaking of the great dam (sadd al-'Arim).

Two gardens producing bitter fruit, tamarisk and some lote-trees: that is, two gardens bearing bitter, ugly produce and tamarisk trees (athl).

That: that is, the substitution. We repaid them for their disbelief.

The towns which We had blessed: these are the towns of Syria, which are blessed.

Visible towns: that is, connected from Yemen to Syria.

And We determined therein the journeys: that is, the distances between them were measured such that they would rest at midday in one town and spend the night in another.

And We made them into tales: that is, for those who came after them. That is, We destroyed them, and nothing remained of them except their remembrance, circulated among people.

And We scattered them with complete dispersal: that is, We dispersed them throughout the lands with total scattering.

Indeed in that are signs: that is, indeed in that mentioned bounty and its removal are lessons.

For every patient, grateful one: that is, patient in obedience and abstaining from sins, grateful for blessings.

Meaning of the verses:

When God mentioned His favour upon the family of Dawud and their thankfulness to Him, and informed that few of His servants are thankful for His favour upon them, He mentioned the descendants of Saba', and that He had bestowed upon them great blessings, but they did not give thanks for them, so He sent down His vengeance upon them, stripped them of His blessing, and that is the recompense of every ungrateful one. God said: ﴿Indeed there was for Saba' in their dwelling a sign: two gardens, on the right and on the left﴾. That is, indeed there was for the descendants of Saba', namely al-Azd, al-Ash'ariyyun, Himyar, Kindah, Madhhij and Anmar, and from Anmar were Ju'um and Bajilah, and from the descendants of Saba' four clans settled in Syria, namely Lakhm, Judham, Ghassan and 'Amilah. Their father Saba' is Saba' ibn Yashjub ibn Ya'rub ibn Qahtan. God's words ﴿in their dwelling﴾ mean in their dwellings, ﴿a sign﴾ meaning a sign of God's power and His bounty upon His servants, and it is two gardens, on the right and the left of the valley, that is, two gardens on the right of the valley and another on its left, all of them fruits and greenery, watered by the water of the Marib dam. ﴿Eat of the provision of your Lord﴾: that is, We said to them, eat of the provision of your Lord and give thanks to Him, that is, for this bounty, by believing in Him and His messengers and obeying Him and His messengers.

God's words ﴿A good land﴾ mean this is a good land, namely Sana'a of Yemen, whose climate is good and whose soil is good, with no plague, no vermin, and no insects such as scorpions and the like there. ﴿And a Lord Forgiving﴾, who forgives your sins whenever you sin, repent, and seek forgiveness. But these blessings made them arrogant, so they disbelieved in them and did not give thanks, as God said: ﴿But they turned away﴾, by denying the messengers of God sent to them and disobeying God and His messengers, so God took vengeance upon them for their turning away and their failure to give thanks, as is His way with His servants. God said: ﴿So We sent upon them the flood of al-'Arim﴾. That was because the dam was destroyed, the waters vanished, the trees died, the land became barren, and they were changed. God said: ﴿And We replaced their two gardens with two gardens producing bitter fruit﴾, that is, bitter, ugly produce, which is the arak tree, and athl, which is the tamarisk, and a little lote-tree.

This is the recompense of one who turns away from the remembrance of God, transgresses His command and departs from His obedience. God said: ﴿That﴾, that is, the recompense, ﴿We repaid them for their disbelief﴾, because of their disbelief. And His words ﴿And do We repay except the ungrateful?﴾ mean: and do We repay with such a recompense, which is turning blessing into vengeance, anyone other than the ungrateful?

God's words: ﴿And We placed between them and the towns which We had blessed﴾, namely the towns of Syria, ﴿visible towns﴾, that is, towns visible on the elevated parts of the land. From Sana'a, their capital, to Syria there were about four thousand seven hundred towns, that is, cities. God's words ﴿And We determined therein the journeys﴾ mean He made the distances between each city and the next close, such that a traveller would set out without provisions of water or food, rest only in one city, leave after the midday rest, and sleep only in another city, until he reached Syria or the city he wished. This was theirs before the dam was destroyed and they were dispersed. God's words: ﴿Travel therein by night and by day, safe﴾: that is, We said to them, travel between those cities by nights and days countless, safe from everything feared. But what they did was that they became arrogant over the blessing and said: ﴿Our Lord, make the distances of our journeys far apart﴾, and they wronged themselves. That is, the arrogance of the blessing led them to ask their Lord, by the tongue of their state or their words, to distance the stages of their journeys by removing those towns, so that they would have to carry provisions, ride horses, and taste the hardship of travel. In reality this was envy by the rich toward the poor, who had no ability to travel long distances without provisions or mounts. God said: ﴿And they wronged themselves﴾, since by their turning away, their envy and their arrogance over the blessing, they had wronged themselves, and so they were exposed to the punishment of deprivation in this world and the punishment of the Fire in the Hereafter. God's words ﴿So We made them into tales﴾ mean for those after them, who relate their reports and recount their stories after they perished and were destroyed. God's words ﴿And We scattered them with complete dispersal﴾ mean We dispersed them throughout the lands with total dispersal, such that no reconnection was hoped for them ever again. So al-Aws and al-Khazraj went to Yathrib, "the Prophet's city" (al-Madinah), and they are the Ansar; Ghassan went to Syria; al-Azd went to 'Uman; and Khuza'ah went to Tihamah, and they became a proverb, and it is said: "They went off in every direction (shadhr madhr)." And "they were scattered as the hands of Saba'" (tafarraqu ayadi Saba'), that is, the ways and paths of Saba'. God's words ﴿Indeed in that are signs﴾ mean indeed in God's bounty upon the sons of Saba', and then in His vengeance upon them when they became arrogant over the blessing and disbelieved in obedience, are lessons by which every one patient in obedience in deed and abstaining from sins in omission is admonished, ﴿grateful﴾, that is, abundant in thanks for blessings. O God, make us among Your grateful servants.

Meaning of the verses:

When God mentioned His favour upon the family of Dawud and their thankfulness to Him, and informed that few of His servants are thankful for His favour upon them, He mentioned the descendants of Saba', and that He had bestowed upon them great blessings, but they did not give thanks for them, so He sent down His vengeance upon them, stripped them of His blessing, and that is the recompense of every ungrateful one. God's words ﴿in their dwelling﴾ mean in their dwellings, ﴿a sign﴾ meaning a sign of God's power and His bounty upon His servants, and it is two gardens, on the right and the left of the valley, that is, two gardens on the right of the valley and another on its left, all of them fruits and greenery, watered by the water of the Marib dam. ﴿Eat of the provision of your Lord﴾: that is, We said to them, eat of the provision of your Lord and give thanks to Him, that is, for this bounty, by believing in Him and His messengers and obeying Him and His messengers.

But these blessings made them arrogant, so they disbelieved in them and did not give thanks, as God said: ﴿But they turned away﴾, by denying the messengers of God sent to them and disobeying God and His messengers, so God took vengeance upon them for their turning away and their failure to give thanks, as is His way with His servants. God said: ﴿That﴾, that is, the recompense, ﴿We repaid them for their disbelief﴾, because of their disbelief. **Commentary of al-Jaza'iri (Aysar al-Tafasir) on Surah 34, verses 20–23**

**Explanation of the words:**

﴿Iblis had indeed found his assumption about them to be true﴾: meaning, Iblis's assumption about them, that he would be able to lead them astray, proved correct.

﴿So they followed him﴾: in disbelief, misguidance, and misguiding others.

﴿Except a group of the believers﴾: that is, of the children of Adam, namely the believing Muslims. They did not follow him, and his assumption about them was proven wrong, and God increased his disappointment until the Day of Resurrection.

﴿And he had no authority over them﴾: that is, God did not give Iblis any power over them, neither by a staff nor by a sword. He only had adornment and enticement toward desires.

﴿Except that We might make evident who believes in the Hereafter from who is in doubt of it﴾: that is, but We permitted him to lead them astray, if he could, through adornment and enticement, so that We might know, with the knowledge of manifestation, who believes and does righteous deeds from who disbelieves and does evil.

﴿And your Lord is Guardian over all things﴾: that is, and your Lord, O Muhammad, is Guardian over all things, and He will recompense people for what they have earned.

﴿Say: Call upon those you claimed besides God﴾: that is, that they are partners with God in His divinity.

﴿They do not possess an atom's weight in the heavens or on the earth﴾: that is, independent ownership in which God does not share with them.

﴿And they have no share in them﴾: that is, they have no partnership in the heavens or on the earth.

﴿And He has no supporter among them﴾: that is, God the Exalted has no helper among your partners whom you call upon, to assist Him in anything.

﴿And intercession with Him does not benefit except for one whom He permits﴾: that is, intercession does not benefit anyone with Him until He Himself gives permission for it.

﴿Until, when fear is removed from their hearts﴾: that is, the fear and dread leave them upon hearing the words of the Lord, the Exalted.

﴿They say: What has your Lord said?﴾: that is, some of them say to others, joyfully, "What has your Lord said?" They reply, "The truth," that is, regarding intercession.

﴿And He is the Most High, the Great﴾: the Most High, above all things in His essence and dominion; He is the Great, the Exalted, to whom everything is subordinate.

**Meaning of the verses:**

When God mentioned what happened to Sheba of changes of fortune, and the cause of that was the adornment and misleading of Satan, He informed about the condition of people, all people, saying: ﴿Iblis had indeed found his assumption about them to be true﴾, meaning, regarding them, since he knew their weakness before desires, so he used the adornment of desires as a weapon against them. ﴿So they followed him﴾ in what he called them to of polytheism, excess, and sins. ﴿Except a group of the believers﴾, and they are the sincere believers in their faith, who submitted their faces to God, and they are the servants of God over whom Satan has no way to mislead them, so they did not follow him. This is what the verse [20] indicates. As for His saying: ﴿And he had no authority over them﴾, that is, Satan had no ﴿authority over them﴾, ﴿except that We might make evident who believes in the Hereafter from who is in doubt of it﴾: that is, neither material strength nor moral strength, in the form of proofs or evidences. Rather, He permitted him only to incite, whisper, and adorn. This permission has a reason, which is the manifestation of the condition of people, so that He may know who believes in the Hereafter and what is in it of gardens and fires. The Garden is surrounded by hardships and the Fire by desires. Those who believe in the Hereafter bear the hardships of obligations, rise to fulfil them, and avoid desires, so they are saved from the Fire and enter the Garden. Those who do not believe in the Hereafter do not rise to any duty and do not avoid what is forbidden, so they lose themselves and their families on the Day of Resurrection, and that is the clear loss.

As for His saying ﴿And your Lord is Guardian over all things﴾, He counts the deeds of His servants, good and bad, holds them accountable for them, and recompenses them for them.

As for His saying: ﴿Say: Call upon those you claimed besides God﴾, that is: Say, O Our Messenger, after this presentation and the conclusive explanation that has preceded in this context, to the polytheists of your people, as long as you persist in polytheism on the pretext that your partners benefit and harm and that they intercede for you on the Day you are raised: call upon them. Yet the truth that you must hear and know, and what you see and desire after that, is that those whom you call upon besides God and whom you have made partners with God do not possess an atom's weight, that is the weight of an atom, in the heavens or on the earth. They do not possess it independently, nor do they possess it in partnership with God, the true Owner. This is the meaning of His saying: ﴿Say: Call upon those you claimed besides God. They do not possess an atom's weight in the heavens or on the earth﴾. ﴿And they have no share in them﴾: that is, in the heavens and the earth, any partnership, even to the smallest degree. Another matter: your partners whom you call upon have no supporter for God, the Exalted, among them, that is, no helper, so that it cannot be said that since the Lord needs them, we call upon them so that they may intercede for us with Him. Another matter: intercession with God does not take effect for anyone and does not occur for him unless God, the Exalted, is pleased with the intercession for the one for whom intercession is sought, and after He also gives permission to the one who wishes to intercede. So there remains no hope whatsoever of your gods interceding for you, neither in this world nor in the Hereafter. Then how is their worship valid, when they do not possess an atom's weight in the heavens or on the earth, and do not intercede for anyone in this world or the Hereafter?

As for His saying ﴿Until, when fear is removed from their hearts﴾ to the end, it explains the manner of intercession on the Day of Resurrection: the intercessor who has been permitted to intercede, when he asks God, the Exalted, and the Lord, the Exalted, responds to him, is struck with fear and intense dread. ﴿Until, when fear is removed from their hearts﴾, that is, that fear and dread departs. They say to one another: ﴿What has your Lord said?﴾, and they answer, rejoicing: ﴿The truth﴾, that is, He has permitted us to intercede. ﴿And He is the Most High, the Great﴾, that is, high above His creation in His essence, His subjugation, and His authority, the Great, to whom nothing is similar. Glorified is He; there is no god but Him, and no lord besides Him.

**Guidance from the verses:**

1. Explanation that Iblis's assumption about the children of Adam proved true, and that they would follow him and be led astray by him.

2. Affirmation of monotheism, that there is no god but God, and that none deserves worship besides Him.

3. Explanation of the invalidity of calling upon other than God, since the one called upon, whoever he is, does not possess an atom's weight in the universe, neither independently nor in partnership. Nor does God have any supporter, meaning no helpers through whom one could seek nearness. Finally, intercession is not realized except by His permission and for whomever He is pleased to permit it. Therefore, calling upon other than God is void. Whoever calls upon other than God, whether a king, a prophet, a saint, or others, has indeed strayed from the path and committed shirk in the greatest act of worship, which is supplication, and we seek refuge with God, the Exalted.

Therefore, calling upon other than God is void. Whoever calls upon other than God, whether a king, a prophet, a saint, or others, has indeed strayed from the path and committed shirk in the greatest act of worship, which is supplication, and we seek refuge with God, the Exalted.

Commentary of al-Jaza'iri (Aysar al-Tafasir) on surah 34, verses 24–30:

Explanation of the words:

﴿Say: Who provides for you from the heavens and the earth?﴾ From the heavens by sending down rain, and from the earth by causing crops to grow.

﴿Say: Allah.﴾ That is: if they do not answer, then you answer, saying "Allah," for they have no answer other than Him.

﴿And indeed, we or you are surely upon guidance or in clear error.﴾ That is: inform them that you, O polytheists, or we are upon guidance or in clear error. Certainly the monotheists are those upon guidance, and the polytheists are in clear error. He only put it in this form of doubt out of gentleness toward them, so that perhaps they will reflect and be guided.

﴿Say: You will not be asked about what we committed of sins.﴾ That is: you will not be asked about our sins.

﴿And we will not be asked about what you do.﴾ That is: and we will not be asked about what you do. This too is out of gentleness toward them, so that they reconsider their affair and the speech does not drive them to obstinacy.

﴿Say: Our Lord will bring us together, then He will judge between us in truth.﴾ That is: say to them, "Our Lord will bring us together on the Day of Resurrection and will decide between us with truth," and this too is gentleness toward them, and it is the truth.

﴿Say: Show me those you have joined to Him as partners.﴾ That is: say to these polytheists, "Show me your partners whom you worshipped besides Allah." If they show Him idols that neither hear nor see, the proof is established against them. And He said to them, "Do you worship what you carve, and leave Allah who created you and what you do?"

﴿No! Rather, He is Allah, the Mighty, the Wise.﴾ No: the idols cannot be fit for worship; rather, the true deity deserving of worship is Allah, the Mighty, the Wise.

﴿Comprehensively for mankind.﴾ That is: for all people, both their Arabs and non-Arabs.

﴿A bringer of good news and a warner.﴾ A bringer of good news to the believers of Paradise, and a warner to the disbelievers of the punishment of the Fire.

﴿Say: For you is an appointment of a Day.﴾ This is the Day of Resurrection.

Meaning of the verses:

The context still concerns rebuking the polytheists and establishing proofs against them by affirming monotheism and refuting their setting up of rivals. Allah the Exalted said to His Messenger ﷺ, "Ask your people in rebuke: ﴿Say: Who provides for you from the heavens and the earth?﴾ By sending down rain, sending winds as fertilizers, causing plants, crops and fruits to grow, and providing livestock for meat, milk and their products?" If they falter in answering or hesitate out of fear of intellectual defeat, then answer yourself, saying, "Allah," for they have no answer other than this.

His saying ﴿And indeed, we or you are surely upon guidance or in clear error﴾ is a style of raising doubt, and its wisdom is gentleness toward the obstinate opponent, so that he does not persist in obstinacy and does not reflect on the matter he disputes. Otherwise, the Messenger and the believers are those upon guidance, and the polytheists are those in clear error, which is a matter agreed upon by both parties to the dispute. His saying, Exalted is He, ﴿Say: You will not be asked about what we committed of sins, and we will not be asked about what you do﴾ is also of the same kind of gentleness toward the obstinate opponent, so that the storm of his obstinacy may subside and he may examine himself, perhaps returning to his right mind and to what is correct. As for ﴿You will not be asked about what we committed﴾, it is true, for they will not be asked about the sins of the Messenger and the believers; but the Messenger and the believers have no sin, and this is only a matter of gentleness in address. As for the polytheists, they have deeds of shirk and falsehood for which they will be recompensed, while the Messenger and the believers are certainly not asked about them and are not held accountable for them, so long as they have conveyed and given sincere counsel.

His saying: ﴿Say: Our Lord will bring us together﴾, that is, on the Day of Resurrection, ﴿then He will judge between us﴾, that is, decide and separate between us, ﴿in truth. And He is the Opener, the All-Knowing﴾, that is, the Judge, the Knower of the conditions of His creation, so His judgments will be just, for His knowledge of what He judges, outwardly and inwardly. In this there is an invitation to them with gentleness and without harshness, so that they may acknowledge the Final Resurrection, which they deny vehemently. His saying ﴿Say: Show me those you have joined to Him as partners﴾, that is, say, O our Messenger, to these polytheists: "Show me your gods whom you have associated with Allah and joined to Him, and whom you said in your talbiyah: 'Here I am, O Allah, here I am; You have no partner, except a partner who belongs to You, You possess him and what he possesses.'" Thus the Messenger of Allah challenges them, by Allah's permission, to show him partners of Allah in reality, who hear, see, benefit and harm. Since it was impossible for them to produce anything other than idols and images, He rebuked them harshly, perhaps they would awaken from their heedlessness, and said: ﴿No! Rather, He is Allah, the Mighty, the Wise﴾, that is, those idols are not gods worshipped besides Allah; rather, the true deity deserving of worship is Allah, Lord of the worlds and God of the first and the last. ﴿The Mighty﴾, that is, the One who prevails in His command and His will, ﴿the Wise﴾ in the management of His creation and the affairs of His servants.

His saying: ﴿And We have not sent you except comprehensively to mankind, as a bringer of good news and a warner﴾, that is, We have not sent you, O our Messenger, for any task other than good news and warning. Therefore, let not their turning away and their non-response grieve you. Give good news to whoever believes in you and follows what you have brought, and warn whoever disbelieves in you and does not follow the guidance to which you call.

His saying: ﴿But most of mankind do not know﴾ contains consolation for the Messenger as well, for the reality is that most people do not know; for had they known, they would not have hesitated to worship Allah, affirm His oneness, and draw near to Him, hoping for what is with Him and fearing what is with Him.

His saying: ﴿And they say﴾, that is, the people of Makkah who deny the Resurrection and the recompense, ﴿When is this promise?﴾, that is, the punishment with which you threaten us and frighten us by its descent upon us, if you believers are truthful in what you tell us and promise us. Here Allah the Exalted commanded His Messenger to answer their mockery and denial by saying: ﴿Say: For you is an appointment of a Day﴾, a specific, determined Day with Us, from which you will not delay an hour if you sought that to repent and seek forgiveness, nor will you advance it an hour if you asked to hasten it, for the matter is decreed and firm, admitting neither reduction, nor increase, nor alteration, nor change.

Guidance from the verses:

1- The legitimacy of gentleness toward the opponent, giving him room in the sphere of thought, perhaps he will return to his right mind.

2- Affirmation of the doctrine of Resurrection and recompense, and varying the methods of calling to it.

3- Affirmation of the doctrine of the prophethood of Muhammad ﷺ, and the universality of the Prophet's ﷺ message to all mankind.

4- The Day of Resurrection is the appointed time of the Hour and the Day, so it is not valid to advance or delay it under any circumstances.

﴿And indeed, we or you are surely upon guidance or in clear error.﴾ That is: inform them that you, O polytheists, or we are upon guidance or in clear error. Certainly the monotheists are those upon guidance, and the polytheists are in clear error. He only put it in this form of doubt out of gentleness toward them, so that perhaps they will reflect and be guided.

﴿Say: You will not be asked about what we committed of sins.﴾ That is: you will not be asked about our sins.

﴿And we will not be asked about what you do.﴾ That is: and we will not be asked about what you do. This too is out of gentleness toward them, so that they reconsider their affair and the speech does not drive them to obstinacy.

﴿Say: Our Lord will bring us together, then He will judge between us in truth.﴾ That is: say to them, "Our Lord will bring us together on the Day of Resurrection and will decide between us with truth," and this too is gentleness toward them, and it is the truth.

﴿Say: Show me those you have joined to Him as partners.﴾ That is: say to these polytheists, "Show me your partners whom you worshipped besides Allah." If they show Him idols that neither hear nor see, the proof is established against them. And He said to them, "Do you worship what you carve, and leave Allah who created you and what you do?"

﴿No! Rather, He is Allah, the Mighty, the Wise.﴾ No: the idols cannot be fit for worship; rather, the true deity deserving of worship is Allah, the Mighty, the Wise.

﴿Comprehensively for mankind.﴾ That is: for all people, both their Arabs and non-Arabs.

﴿A bringer of good news and a warner.﴾ A bringer of good news to the believers of Paradise, and a warner to the disbelievers of the punishment of the Fire.

﴿Say: For you is an appointment of a Day.﴾ This is the Day of Resurrection.

Meaning of the verses:

The context still concerns rebuking the polytheists and establishing proofs against them by affirming monotheism and refuting their setting up of rivals. Allah the Exalted said to His Messenger ﷺ, "Ask your people in rebuke: ﴿Say: Who provides for you from the heavens and the earth?﴾ By sending down rain, sending winds as fertilizers, causing plants, crops and fruits to grow, and providing livestock for meat, milk and their products?" If they falter in answering or hesitate out of fear of intellectual defeat, then answer yourself, saying, "Allah," for they have no answer other than this.

His saying ﴿And indeed, we or you are surely upon guidance or in clear error﴾ is a style of raising doubt, and its wisdom is gentleness toward the obstinate opponent, so that he does not persist in obstinacy and does not reflect on the matter he disputes. Otherwise, the Messenger and the believers are those upon guidance, and the polytheists are those in clear error, which is a matter agreed upon by both parties to the dispute. His saying, Exalted is He, ﴿Say: You will not be asked about what we committed of sins, and we will not be asked about what you do﴾ is also of the same kind of gentleness toward the obstinate opponent, so that the storm of his obstinacy may subside and he may examine himself, perhaps returning to his right mind and to what is correct. As for ﴿You will not be asked about what we committed﴾, it is true, for they will not be asked about the sins of the Messenger and the believers; but the Messenger and the believers have no sin, and this is only a matter of gentleness in address. As for the polytheists, they have deeds of shirk and falsehood for which they will be recompensed, while the Messenger and the believers are certainly not asked about them and are not held accountable for them, so long as they have conveyed and given sincere counsel.

His saying: ﴿Say: Our Lord will bring us together﴾, that is, on the Day of Resurrection, ﴿then He will judge between us﴾, that is, decide and separate between us, ﴿in truth. And He is the Opener, the All-Knowing﴾, that is, the Judge, the Knower of the conditions of His creation, so His judgments will be just, for His knowledge of what He judges, outwardly and inwardly. In this there is an invitation to them with gentleness and without harshness, so that they may acknowledge the Final Resurrection, which they deny vehemently. His saying ﴿Say: Show me those you have joined to Him as partners﴾, that is, say, O our Messenger, to these polytheists: "Show me your gods whom you have associated with Allah and joined to Him, and whom you said in your talbiyah: 'Here I am, O Allah, here I am; You have no partner, except a partner who belongs to You, You possess him and what he possesses.'" Thus the Messenger of Allah challenges them, by Allah's permission, to show him partners of Allah in reality, who hear, see, benefit and harm. Since it was impossible for them to produce anything other than idols and images, He rebuked them harshly, perhaps they would awaken from their heedlessness, and said: ﴿No! Rather, He is Allah, the Mighty, the Wise﴾, that is, those idols are not gods worshipped besides Allah; rather, the true deity deserving of worship is Allah, Lord of the worlds and God of the first and the last. ﴿The Mighty﴾, that is, the One who prevails in His command and His will, ﴿the Wise﴾ in the management of His creation and the affairs of His servants.

His saying: ﴿And We have not sent you except comprehensively to mankind, as a bringer of good news and a warner﴾, that is, We have not sent you, O our Messenger, for any task other than good news and warning. Therefore, let not their turning away and their non-response grieve you. Give good news to whoever believes in you and follows what you have brought, and warn whoever disbelieves in you and does not follow the guidance to which you call.

His saying: ﴿But most of mankind do not know﴾ contains consolation for the Messenger as well, for the reality is that most people do not know; for had they known, they would not have hesitated to worship Allah, affirm His oneness, and draw near to Him, hoping for what is with Him and fearing what is with Him.

His saying: ﴿And they say﴾, that is, the people of Makkah who deny the Resurrection and the recompense, ﴿When is this promise?﴾, that is, the punishment with which you threaten us and frighten us by its descent upon us, if you believers are truthful in what you tell us and promise us. Here Allah the Exalted commanded His Messenger to answer their mockery and denial by saying: ﴿Say: For you is an appointment of a Day﴾, a specific, determined Day with Us, from which you will not delay an hour if you sought that to repent and seek forgiveness, nor will you advance it an hour if you asked to hasten it, for the matter is decreed and firm, admitting neither reduction, nor increase, nor alteration, nor change.

Guidance from the verses:

1- The legitimacy of gentleness toward the opponent, giving him room in the sphere of thought, perhaps he will return to his right mind.

2- Affirmation of the doctrine of Resurrection and recompense, and varying the methods of calling to it.

3- Affirmation of the doctrine of the prophethood of Muhammad ﷺ, and the universality of the Prophet's ﷺ message to all mankind.

4- The Day of Resurrection is the appointed time of the Hour and the Day, so it is not valid to advance or delay it under any circumstances.

**Commentary of al-Jaza'iri (Aysar al-Tafasir) on Surah 34, verses 31–33**

**Explanation of the words:**

*"Nor in what was before it"*: meaning the earlier scriptures, namely the Torah and the Gospel.

*"Some of them will refer back the speech to others"*: meaning the followers will say such-and-such, and the leaders will answer them with such-and-such, as is shown in the verses.

*"Did we avert you from guidance?"*: meaning the arrogant, who are the leaders, deny that they turned their followers away from guidance after it had come to them through His Messenger.

*"Rather, you were criminals"*: meaning wrongdoers, corrupt and corrupting.

*"Rather, it was the plotting of the night and the day"*: meaning the matter is not as you claim. Rather, your plotting against us by night and day is what caused us to disbelieve in Allah.

*"And We set up rivals to Him"*: meaning partners whom we worshipped besides Him, thereby rivaling Him with them.

*"And they concealed the regret"*: meaning they hid it, since regret would be of no benefit, or they displayed it. The phrase *asarru al-nadama* ("they concealed the regret") has two meanings: "they hid it" and "they showed it."

*"And We put the shackles on the necks"*: *al-aghlal* is the plural of *ghull*, an iron collar placed around the neck of a criminal.

*"Are they recompensed except for what they used to do?"*: meaning they are recompensed only for what they used to do.

**Meaning of the verses:**

The noble context continues to establish *al-tawhid* (the affirmation of God's oneness), *al-ba'th* (resurrection), and *al-jaza'* (recompense). Allah, the Exalted, says: ﴿And those who disbelieved said﴾, meaning some of the polytheists of Makkah said to the Messenger and the believers, "We will never believe in this Qur'an that was revealed to Muhammad, nor in what was revealed before it, such as the Torah and the Gospel." This is because when they were argued against with the Torah and the Gospel, which affirm monotheism, prophethood, resurrection, and recompense, they said, "We will never believe in all of it," out of obstinacy, arrogance, denial, and wrongdoing. The implication of this is that they are wrongdoers who are stubbornly opposed. As part of calling them to guidance, the verses now present their condition on the Day of Resurrection. Allah, the Exalted, says to His Messenger while they are listening: ﴿If only you could see﴾, O Our Messenger, ﴿when the wrongdoers are made to stand before their Lord, returning speech to one another﴾, meaning they argue with each other, blaming one another. Those who were oppressed, namely the poor and subordinate who were followers of their elders and wealthy ones, will say to those who were arrogant toward them in the world: "Were it not for you, you would have diverted us from faith and from following the Messenger, and we would have been believers." The elders will answer them with what Allah, the Exalted, reported in His saying: ﴿Those who were arrogant will say to those who were oppressed, "Did we avert you from guidance after it had come to you?"﴾, meaning, "We never averted you at all. Rather, you were criminals," that is, people of crime and corruption. The oppressed will answer them, speaking as Allah, the Exalted, reported about them: ﴿And those who were oppressed will say to those who were arrogant, "Rather, it was your plotting by night and day, when you ordered us to disbelieve in Allah and set up rivals to Him."﴾ Allah, the Exalted, said: ﴿And they concealed the regret﴾, meaning they hid it when they saw the punishment. Allah, the Exalted, said: ﴿And We put the shackles on the necks of those who disbelieved﴾, meaning their hands were tied to their necks with shackles, which are the plural of *ghull*, an iron collar with which a criminal is bound. Then they were cast into Hellfire, as they were in a place outside of them. His saying, the Exalted, ﴿Are they recompensed except for what they used to do?﴾ means they are recompensed only for what they used to do. So recompense corresponds to deeds: if they were good, the recompense is good, and if they were evil, the recompense is evil. Their deeds were all evil, wrongdoing, and falsehood.

Furthermore, the answer to *law* ("if only") at the beginning of the context is omitted and can be estimated as: "you would have seen a dreadful matter." The omission is because presenting their standing is enough, and mentioning the answer is unnecessary, as this is more complete and comprehensive.

**Guidance from the verses:**

1. The condition of the wrongdoers and criminals is similar. The idolaters of Arabia used to lean on the People of the Book and argue against the Messenger and the believers using what they had. When they found that the Torah and the Gospel affirmed the belief in resurrection, recompense, and prophethood, they disowned them and said, "We will not believe in the Qur'an, nor in the Torah and the Gospel."

The Jews used to argue against the Muslims using the Torah. When they found that the Torah affirmed what the Qur'an affirms, they abandoned arguing with the Torah and began arguing with magic, as was mentioned in al-Baqarah in the saying of Allah, the Exalted: ﴿And when there came to them a messenger from Allah confirming what was with them, a party of those who were given the Scripture threw the Book of Allah behind their backs as if they did not know, and followed what the devils recited during the reign of Solomon﴾ [Al-Baqarah: 101–102].

2. The affirmation of the belief in resurrection and recompense through a complete presentation of one of the scenes of the Day of Resurrection and one of its sights.

3. The invalidity of people's argument by the deeds of scholars, wise men, or nobles when those deeds do not conform to the law of Allah, the Exalted, and to what His messengers brought of the truth and the correct religion.

Commentary of al-Jaza'iri (Aysar al-Tafasir) on surah 34, verses 34–39:

Explanation of the words:

"إلا قال مترفوها" (But its affluent ones said): i.e., its leaders who were blessed with wealth and standing among the people of property and status.

"نحن أكثر أموالاً وأولاداً" (We have more wealth and children): i.e., than the believers.

"يبسط الرزق لمن يشاء" (He extends provision to whomever He wills): as a test, whether the servant will be grateful or ungrateful.

"ويقدر" (and restricts it): i.e., He constricts it as a trial, whether a person will be patient or resentful.

"ولكن أكثر الناس لا يعلمون" (But most people do not know): i.e., the wisdom in expanding provision for some and restricting it for others.

"تقربكم عندنا زلفى" (bring you near to Us in nearness): i.e., nearness, meaning bringing close.

"إلا من آمن وعمل صالحا" (except one who believes and does righteous deeds): i.e., but the one who believes and does righteous deeds is the one whom We bring near.

"وهم في الغرفات آمنون" (and they will be secure in the upper chambers): i.e., safe from illness, death, and every hardship.

"والذين سعوا في آياتنا" (And those who strive against Our verses): i.e., who work to nullify the Qur'an, to disbelieve in it, and to refuse its judgment.

"معاجزين" (seeking to frustrate): i.e., assuming that they have outdone Us, so that We would not punish them.

"وما أنفقتم من شيء" (And whatever you spend of anything): i.e., of wealth spent in good.

"وهو خير الرازقين" (and He is the best of providers): i.e., the best of those who grant provision. As for the creation of provision, it belongs to Allah the Exalted alone.

Explanation of the verses:

Allah the Exalted says: "﴿وَمَا أَرْسَلْنَا فِي قَرْيَةٍ مِّن نَّذِيرٍ﴾" (And We did not send into any town a warner). This begins consoling the Messenger (ﷺ) by showing the condition of the nations before him and how they confronted their messengers. He says: "﴿وَمَا أَرْسَلْنَا فِي قَرْيَةٍ﴾" (And We did not send into a town), i.e., any city, "﴿مِّن نَّذِيرٍ إِلَّا قَالَ مُتْرَفُوهَا﴾" (but its affluent ones said), i.e., the people of wealth and abundance who indulge in various foods, drinks, clothing, and mounts.

They said to Allah's messengers: "﴿إِنَّا بِمَا أُرْسِلْتُم بِهِ كَافِرُونَ﴾" (Indeed, we disbelieve in what you have been sent with), thereby rejecting their call. "﴿وَقَالُوا نَحْنُ أَكْثَرُ أَمْوَالًا وَأَوْلَادًا﴾" (And they said, "We have more wealth and children"), taking pride in their strength. "﴿وَمَا نَحْنُ بِمُعَذَّبِينَ﴾" (And we will not be punished) — they denied resurrection and recompense. Their speech also indicates that they were deceived into thinking that what Allah gave them of wealth and children was a sign of His pleasure with them and that He was not angry with them. As for His saying: "﴿قُلْ إِنَّ رَبِّي يَبْسُطُ الرِّزْقَ لِمَن يَشَاءُ وَيَقْدِرُ﴾" (Say, "Indeed, my Lord extends provision to whom He wills and restricts it"), i.e., say, O our Prophet, to those deceived ones who think that what they have of wealth and children results from Allah's pleasure with them: Say to them, "Indeed my Lord, majestic in His majesty, extends provision to whom He wills as a test for him, not as a sign of His pleasure with him nor of His hatred for him, just as He restricts provision for whom He wills as a trial, not because of His hatred or His love." "﴿وَلَٰكِنَّ أَكْثَرَ النَّاسِ لَا يَعْلَمُونَ﴾" (But most people do not know) — among them the polytheists of Quraysh — that the extension of provision, like its restriction, returns to the training of people through ease and hardship, as a test and a trial.

As for His saying: "﴿وَمَا أَمْوَالُكُمْ وَلَا أَوْلَادُكُم بِالَّتِي تُقَرِّبُكُمْ عِندَنَا زُلْفَىٰ﴾" (And neither your wealth nor your children are that which will bring you near to Us in nearness), Allah the Exalted informs the polytheists who are deceived by wealth and children, saying to them: your wealth and your children are not of the state that brings you near to Us, makes Us pleased with you, and draws you close to Us in nearness. "﴿إِلَّا مَنْ آمَنَ وَعَمِلَ صَالِحًا﴾" (Except one who believes and does righteous deeds), i.e., but those who perform the obligatory and recommended acts. Commentary of al-Jaza'iri (Aysar al-Tafasir) on surah 34, verses 40–42:

Explanation of the words:

﻿"And the day He gathers them all together": i.e., remember the day We gather them all together, that is, all the polytheists.

"Did these worship you?": i.e., the Exalted says this to the angels as a rebuke and reproach to the polytheists.

"They will say: Glory be to You": i.e., the angels say, "Glory be to You," meaning exalting You above association (shirk) and declaring You far above it.

"You are our Guardian, not them": i.e., there is no alliance between us and them; that is, they disown them.

"Rather, they used to worship the jinn": i.e., the devils who would appear to them in forms that they took to be angels, so they obeyed them, and that was their worship of them.

"So today none of you has power for another, to benefit or to harm": i.e., the objects of worship have no power to benefit their worshippers nor to harm them.

"And We will say to those who wronged": i.e., those who associated others with God in worship, such as the angels, the prophets, or the saints and righteous.

"Taste the punishment of the Fire which you used to deny": i.e., in the world you used to deny the Resurrection and the recompense, which is Paradise or the Fire.

The meaning of the verses:

The noble context continues to establish the doctrines of resurrection, recompense, and monotheism. The Almighty said to His Messenger ﷺ, "Remember" the Day when He gathers them ("وَيَوْمَ يَحْشُرُهُمْ") — that is, the polytheists — "all together" ("جَمِيعًا"), so We leave none of them behind.
