**Explanation of the Words:**

*Ayatuna bayyinat* (ﷻ): That is, the verses of the Noble Qur'an are clear, evident in meaning, and plain in their indication.

*Qalu ma hadha illa rajul* (﴿they said: "This is only a man"﴾): That is, Muhammad is only a man from among men.

*Yurid an yasuddakum 'amma kana ya'budu aba'ukum* (﴿he wants to turn you away from what your fathers worshipped﴾): That is, he wants to turn you away from worshipping your gods, which your fathers worshipped before you.

*Illa ifk muftara* (﴿only a fabricated lie﴾): That is, only a invented, forged lie.

*Wa qala alladhina kafaru lil-haqqi lamma ja'ahum* (﴿those who disbelieved said of the truth when it came to them﴾): That is, they said of the Qur'an, when Muhammad (ﷺ) brought it to them.

*In hadha illa sihr mubin* (﴿this is nothing but clear magic﴾): That is, this, meaning the Qur'an, is nothing but clear magic; that is, Muhammad is a magician and the Qur'an is magic.

*Min kutubin yadrusunaha* (﴿from books which they study﴾): That is, which they read, and which permitted them to associate partners with God and gave them leave to do so.

*Wa ma arsalna ilayhim qablaka min nadhir* (﴿We did not send to them before you any warner﴾): That is, We did not send to them before you any messenger who called them to polytheism.

*Wa ma balaghu ma'shara ma ataynahum* (﴿nor have they attained a tenth of what We gave them﴾): That is, those past nations whom We destroyed did not attain a tenth of what We gave these people of proofs and clear evidences.

*Fa kayfa kana nakir* (﴿how was My rejection?﴾): That is, how was My condemnation of them, by punishment and destruction? The response was fitting and did not miss its mark in any way.

**Meaning of the Verses:**

The context continues to present the shameful positions of the polytheists, to denounce them, and to threaten them severely. God, the Exalted, says: ﴿And when Our verses are recited to them﴾, that is, to the polytheists of Quraysh and their disbelievers, ﴿clear verses﴾, that is, recited by Our Messenger, clear in indication and manifest in meaning regarding what he calls to of truth and denounces of falsehood, their response was to say: ﴿This is only a man who wants to turn you away from what your fathers worshipped.﴾ That is, Muhammad is only a man, not an angel or a king, who wants to turn you away from what your fathers worshipped of idols and stones. Glory be to God! Where do the minds of the polytheists go? Are they not ashamed of what they say about "what your fathers worshipped" of idols and images? He truly turns you away from worshipping idols, but toward worshipping the Most Merciful.

They also said, as God, the Exalted, reports about them in His saying: ﴿This is nothing but a fabricated lie﴾, or a falsehood, ﴿invented﴾, that is, he invented it and fabricated it from himself. That is, they said about the Qur'an and what it contains of legislation, guidance, and light, that Muhammad (ﷺ) had forged it. Glory be to God, how great is the foolishness of these polytheists!

They also said, as God, the Exalted, reports about them in His saying: ﴿And those who disbelieved said of the truth when it came to them: "This is nothing but clear magic."﴾ That is, they said about the Messenger and what he brought them of the call to monotheism and reform, ﴿This is nothing but clear magic﴾, and that was because they saw the influence of the Messenger and the Qur'an on their souls, for it stirred their souls and shook them violently.

After this presentation of the positions of the polytheists, God, the Exalted, says: ﴿And We did not give them any books which they study﴾, that is, the polytheists of Quraysh, ﴿and We did not send to them any warner before you﴾. That is, they insisted on polytheism, and We had not given them books which they read, in which they found permission for polytheism or its legitimacy, so they held firmly to it; and We had not sent to them any messenger before you who permitted them polytheism or set a precedent for them so that they follow his way. By no means, neither this nor that.

So how, then, is this insistence on polytheism, which is falsehood that no book has descended with and no messenger has been sent with?

God, the Exalted, says: ﴿And those before them denied﴾, that is, the perished nations, ﴿and these have not attained a tenth of what those had﴾, that is, these people have not reached a tenth of the strength that those destroyed peoples possessed, and despite that, We destroyed them. ﴿So how was My rejection?﴾ That is, how was My condemnation of them for polytheism and for denying My messengers, by their annihilation and uprooting. Will these weak ones not fear that Our punishment will befall them, so that We destroy them completely as We destroyed those before them? Since God did not desire their annihilation, although they deserved it through denying His Messenger and persisting in polytheism and disbelief, He said to His Messenger: Say to them: ﴿I only admonish you with one thing﴾, that is, with one quality, which is that you stand before God, stripped of desire and partisanship, ﴿two by two﴾, that is, two and two, ﴿and one by one﴾, that is, individually, and then reflect on the life of Muhammad (ﷺ), his noble conduct with you, and his distance from every harm, evil, and corruption. For you certainly know with certainty that there is no madness or jinn in your companion Muhammad. He is only a warner to you before a severe punishment; that is, he (ﷺ) is only a warner to you before a severe punishment that may befall you, and he is compassionate toward you in that, fearful for you, and does not wish it upon you.

**Guidance of the Verses:**

Among the guidance of these verses:

1. The explanation of the obstinacy of the polytheists, the foolishness of their minds, and their intellectual decline.
2. The weakness, harshness, and arrogance of the disbelievers of Quraysh when compared with the earlier nations, for they do not possess even one part in a thousand of their strength, since *al-ma'shar* (one-tenth) is one-tenth of one-tenth of one-tenth.

*Yurid an yasuddakum 'amma kana ya'budu aba'ukum* (﴿he wants to turn you away from what your fathers worshipped﴾): That is, he wants to turn you away from worshipping your gods, which your fathers worshipped before you.

*Wa qala alladhina kafaru lil-haqqi lamma ja'ahum* (﴿those who disbelieved said of the truth when it came to them﴾): That is, they said of the Qur'an, when Muhammad (ﷺ) brought it to them.

**Commentary of al-Jaza'iri (Aysar al-Tafasir) on Surah 34, verses 47–54**

**Explanation of the words:**

**"Say: Indeed, my Lord casts the truth"**: that is, He throws down the true revelation upon His prophets. And He casts the truth against falsehood, so it crushes it.

**"Falsehood neither originates anything nor restores"**: that is, falsehood, which is disbelief, does not originate anything, and does not restore anything; that is, it has no effect.

**"Then if I go astray, I only go astray to my own detriment"**: that is, the sin of my error falls on myself. No one else will be called to account or punished for it.

**"Indeed, He is Hearing, Near"**: that is, He hears what I say to you and is near, not distant, so none of His creation can escape His requital.

**"If you could see when they are terrified, but there is no escape"**: that is, when they are terrified at the Resurrection, they fear and flee, but there is no escape for them from Us; rather they are in Our grip.

**"And they will reach for [faith] from a distant place"**: that is, when they witness the punishment, they will say, "We believe in the Qur'an." But how can they have that, when they are far away? They are in the Hereafter, while faith belongs to the world.

**(al-Tanawush)**: the reaching for something from a distant place.

**"As was done with their likes before"**: that is, We did to them as We did to those before them from the nations of disbelief and falsehood.

**"In disquieting doubt"**: that is, in a doubt that extremely unsettled them, so they became agitated and never found peace in anything.

**Meaning of the verses:**

When the polytheists persisted in dispute and obstinacy, and Allah, exalted is He, invited them to the best solution, which is that they should stand up, free of whim and partisanship, for Allah's sake, in pairs or individually (since a group is prone to disagreement over opinions), and then reflect on the life of the Messenger and what he called them to of guidance and truth, [they would know that] you know that he is not as you accuse him of being, mad. Rather, he is a warner to you before a severe punishment whose occurrence and descent upon you you fear. Here, He commanded him to say to them: "And be a warner to you of what I fear for you. I do not ask you for a wage for warning you," ﴿My reward is only from Allah, and He is over all things Witness﴾, that is, the One who observes me, who knows my truthfulness, and who will reward me for warning you, since He charged me with it and I carried it out in obedience to Him.

His saying, exalted is He, ﴿Say: Indeed, my Lord casts the truth﴾, that is, say to them, O our Messenger: indeed my Lord casts the truth, that is, throws down the revelation upon whomever He wills of His servants. ﴿He is the Knower of the unseen﴾, that is, He is the Knower of the unseen. He knows who is fit to receive revelation and to be sent, so He reveals to him and sends him, just as He revealed to me and sent me to you as a warner and a bearer of good news.

His saying, exalted is He: ﴿Say: The truth has come, and falsehood neither originates nor restores﴾, that is, say to them, O our Messenger: the truth has come, which is Islam, the true religion, so no place or room remains for falsehood, which is polytheism and disbelief. "Falsehood neither originates nor restores": that is, just as it does not originate, it does not restore; it is gone and has no trace at all. And His saying: ﴿Say: If I go astray, I only go astray to my own detriment﴾, that is, inform them that if you go astray in what you stand upon and call to, then the harm of your error returns only to you, not to them. And if you are guided, then your guidance is by the grace of what is revealed to you from your Lord of guidance and light. ﴿Indeed, He is Hearing, Near﴾, Hearing of your words and the words of others, near and not distant, so none of His servants can escape His requital, whether the one who does good is repaid with good, or the one who does evil is repaid with evil.

His saying, exalted is He: ﴿And if you could see when they are terrified, but there is no escape, and they will be seized from a near place﴾, that is, you would see a decisive matter. Allah, exalted is He, says to His Messenger: if you could see when the polytheists are terrified in the courts of the decisive judgment on the Day of Resurrection, terrified from the intensity of the horror and fear, and they are seized from a near place and cast into Hell, you would see a dreadful matter of extreme awfulness. His saying, ﴿but there is no escape﴾, means they will not escape Allah, exalted is He, and will not flee from His grip.

His saying, exalted is He: ﴿And they will say, "We believe in Him"﴾, that is, they will say after they are raised and terrified by the horror of the Resurrection: "We believe in Him," that is, in Allah, His Book, His meeting, and His Messenger. He, exalted is He, says: ﴿And how can they reach [faith]?﴾, that is, how can they reach for faith from a distant place, since they are in the Hereafter while faith was in the world? How could they reach it with such ease, have it accepted from them, and be saved from the punishment? This is very far-fetched and will never happen. And they had disbelieved in it before, that is, especially since faith was presented to them while they were able to accept it, and they rejected it. So how could they now be granted it?

His saying: ﴿And they had been casting [accusations] about the unseen from a distant place﴾, that is, and here they are today in the world, casting about the unseen against Muhammad ﷺ with back-breaking claims: at one time they say he is a liar, at another a sorcerer, at another a poet, and at another mad. All of this is conjecture about the unseen, for which they have no justification and no slightest doubt that could prompt them to it. Finally, He, exalted is He, said: ﴿And a barrier will be placed between them and what they desire﴾, which is faith that brings salvation, ﴿as was done with their likes﴾, that is, their counterparts and helpers among the people of disbelief and denial. When the punishment came to them they said, "We believe," but their faith did not benefit them, and they were destroyed and cast into the blazing Hell. And His saying: ﴿Indeed, they were in disquieting doubt﴾, that is, the polytheists and disbelievers of Quraysh. He, exalted is He, informed that they were in the world in doubt about Our oneness, our Prophet, and our meeting, a doubt that brought them to agitation and unrest. So they did not believe, and died in disbelief and polytheism. This is the recompense of whoever dies in polytheism and disbelief.

**Guidance of the verses:**

1. The one who calls to Allah should not take a wage for it, and should seek his reward from Allah, exalted and mighty is He.
2. Demonstration of the truthfulness of Allah, exalted is He, in His saying: "The truth has come, and falsehood neither originates nor restores," for it is nothing but a fading illusion, and Islam has taken firm root in the Arabian Peninsula, so no religion remains there except Islam.
3. Faith that comes under compulsion does not benefit its possessor, like the faith of one who has seen the punishment.
4. Doubt is disbelief, and there is no faith in the presence of the sight of punishment.

Rather, he is a warner to you before a severe punishment whose occurrence and descent upon you you fear. Here, He commanded him to say to them: "And be a warner to you of what I fear for you. I do not ask you for a wage for warning you," ﴿My reward is only from Allah, and He is over all things Witness﴾, that is, the One who observes me, who knows my truthfulness, and who will reward me for warning you, since He charged me with it and I carried it out in obedience to Him.

His saying, exalted is He, ﴿Say: Indeed, my Lord casts the truth﴾, that is, say to them, O our Messenger: indeed my Lord casts the truth, that is, throws down the revelation upon whomever He wills of His servants. ﴿He is the Knower of the unseen﴾, that is, He is the Knower of the unseen. He knows who is fit to receive revelation and to be sent, so He reveals to him and sends him, just as He revealed to me and sent me to you as a warner and a bearer of good news.

His saying, exalted is He: ﴿Say: The truth has come, and falsehood neither originates nor restores﴾, that is, say to them, O our Messenger: the truth has come, which is Islam, the true religion, so no place or room remains for falsehood, which is polytheism and disbelief. "Falsehood neither originates nor restores": that is, just as it does not originate, it does not restore; it is gone and has no trace at all. And His saying: ﴿Say: If I go astray, I only go astray to my own detriment﴾, that is, inform them that if you go astray in what you stand upon and call to, then the harm of your error returns only to you, not to them. And if you are guided, then your guidance is by the grace of what is revealed to you from your Lord of guidance and light. ﴿Indeed, He is Hearing, Near﴾, Hearing of your words and the words of others, near and not distant, so none of His servants can escape His requital, whether the one who does good is repaid with good, or the one who does evil is repaid with evil.

His saying, exalted is He: ﴿And if you could see when they are terrified, but there is no escape, and they will be seized from a near place﴾, that is, you would see a decisive matter. Allah, exalted is He, says to His Messenger: if you could see when the polytheists are terrified in the courts of the decisive judgment on the Day of Resurrection, terrified from the intensity of the horror and fear, and they are seized from a near place and cast into Hell, you would see a dreadful matter of extreme awfulness. His saying, ﴿but there is no escape﴾, means they will not escape Allah, exalted is He, and will not flee from His grip.

His saying, exalted is He: ﴿And they will say, "We believe in Him"﴾, that is, they will say after they are raised and terrified by the horror of the Resurrection: "We believe in Him," that is, in Allah, His Book, His meeting, and His Messenger. He, exalted is He, says: ﴿And how can they reach [faith]?﴾, that is, how can they reach for faith from a distant place, since they are in the Hereafter while faith was in the world? How could they reach it with such ease, have it accepted from them, and be saved from the punishment? This is very far-fetched and will never happen. And they had disbelieved in it before, that is, especially since faith was presented to them while they were able to accept it, and they rejected it. So how could they now be granted it?

His saying: ﴿And they had been casting [accusations] about the unseen from a distant place﴾, that is, and here they are today in the world, casting about the unseen against Muhammad ﷺ with back-breaking claims: at one time they say he is a liar, at another a sorcerer, at another a poet, and at another mad. All of this is conjecture about the unseen, for which they have no justification and no slightest doubt that could prompt them to it. Finally, He, exalted is He, said: ﴿And a barrier will be placed between them and what they desire﴾, which is faith that brings salvation, ﴿as was done with their likes﴾, that is, their counterparts and helpers among the people of disbelief and denial. When the punishment came to them they said, "We believe," but their faith did not benefit them, and they were destroyed and cast into the blazing Hell. And His saying: ﴿Indeed, they were in disquieting doubt﴾, that is, the polytheists and disbelievers of Quraysh. He, exalted is He, informed that they were in the world in doubt about Our oneness, our Prophet, and our meeting, a doubt that brought them to agitation and unrest. So they did not believe, and died in disbelief and polytheism. This is the recompense of whoever dies in polytheism and disbelief.

**Guidance of the verses:**

1. The one who calls to Allah should not take a wage for it, and should seek his reward from Allah, exalted and mighty is He.
2. Demonstration of the truthfulness of Allah, exalted is He, in His saying: "The truth has come, and falsehood neither originates nor restores," for it is nothing but a fading illusion, and Islam has taken firm root in the Arabian Peninsula, so no religion remains there except Islam.
3. Faith that comes under compulsion does not benefit its possessor, like the faith of one who has seen the punishment.
4. Doubt is disbelief, and there is no faith in the presence of the sight of punishment.
